units.function: Embedded-PostgreSQL route compatibility suite ensuring Issue list and blocked-count APIs accept parentIssueId as an alias for canonical parentId.
units.dependencyDirection: Exercises public company-scoped Issue routes through the shared real-database harness; HTTP query normalization feeds the same list/count persistence filters.
units.keyDataModels: Company-scoped Issue hierarchy, parentId, compatibility parentIssueId, Issue status and blocked attention count.
units.lifecycle: Seed two parent subtrees; query list or blocked count using canonical, alias, both or neither parameter; canonical parentId wins when both differ.
units.testAssessment: Six integration cases cover list/count parity, canonical precedence and no-filter behavior. All skipped locally because embedded PostgreSQL was unavailable. Missing are foreign-parent probes, malformed/empty/repeated parameters, conflict warning/error semantics, deprecation telemetry and version removal policy.
units.designRationale: Preserve existing client compatibility after a query-field naming mismatch while maintaining one effective internal filter.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs explicit, low-risk API compatibility and deprecation rules as its Web, mobile clients and Connectors evolve independently.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE ONLY. Keep one canonical Company OS field and, only when an actual released client requires it, add a thin boundary alias with contract tests, versioned deprecation metadata and usage telemetry. Reject conflicting values with a stable code instead of silently preferring one; validate opaque IDs and tenant visibility before query execution.
units.responsibilityConflict: No direct responsibility-model conflict, but silently resolving conflicting parent identifiers can make an operator or Connector act on a different work subtree than intended and weakens audit explainability.

units.securityFindings: MEDIUM ambiguity: conflicting canonical and alias values are silently accepted, which can conceal a client bug or intent mismatch. MEDIUM coverage gap: foreign-tenant parent IDs and malformed/repeated query values are untested. LOW lifecycle gap: no observable deprecation/version policy. POSITIVE: list and count share deterministic behavior and all returned rows remain company-route scoped in the fixture. TEST LIMITATION: all six focused tests skipped on this host.
